in_arabic.name: أيها
in_arabic.meaning: Interjection used to express sadness, surprise, or calling someone.
in_arabic.long_meaning: The Arabic interjection 'أيها' (Eihaa) is often translated as 'Alas!' or 'Ah!' in English. It is used to express various emotions such as sadness, surprise, or to call someone. It can also be used to express sympathy or consolation.

in_urdu.name: ایہا
in_urdu.meaning: ایک شکاوت یا ترسدوری کا اظہار
in_urdu.long_meaning: In Urdu, 'Eihaa' (ایہا) is pronounced the same as in Arabic and is used with similar meanings. It can be translated to English as 'Alas!', 'Ah!', or 'Oh no!'. It is an expression of sadness, surprise, or calling someone.

in_hindi.name: ऐहा
in_hindi.meaning: एक शोक या तरस का अर्थ
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, 'Eihaa' (ऐहा) is pronounced similarly to the Arabic and Urdu pronunciations and has similar meanings. It can be translated to English as 'Alas!', 'Ah!', or 'Oh no!'. It is an expression of sadness, surprise, or calling someone.

in_pashto.long_meaning: In Pashto, 'Eihaa' (ایها) is pronounced the same as in Arabic, Urdu, and Hindi, and has similar meanings. It can be translated to English as 'Alas!', 'Ah!', or 'Oh no!'. It is an expression of sadness, surprise, or calling someone.
